Cwp-27284-2016
 Date of Decision : 11.07.2024
Subhash Sharma & Ors. .....Petitioners
Versus STATE OF HARYANA & ORS. .....
Respondents CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SURESHWAR THAKUR  HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE SUDEEPTI SHARMA
Present : None for the petitioners.
Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl. A.G., Haryana with  Mr. Saurabh Mago, DAG, Haryana.

** **
SURESHWAR THAKUR, J. (Oral)
1. This Court had been consistently noticing that the Registry of this Court is not preparing the index detailing thereins the pages where exist the documents appended with the writ petition.

Therefore,
the Registry of this Court is directed to ensure both the preparation of an index besides the same being placed at the beginning of the writ petition(s), thus detailing thereins the pages where all the documents exist.
The said directions be ensured to be forthwith complied with.

2. The present petitioners claim relief for quashing of notification bearing No. LAC (G)
NTLA-2003/953 dated 04.11.2003 (Annexure P-3).
Moreover, they also seek quashing of notification bearing No. LAC (G) - NTLA-2004/1113 dated 03.11.2004 (Annexure P-4).

The above said notification(s) are respectively issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter for 1 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086166-DB short called as the 'Act of Subhash Sharma & Ors vs State Of Haryana & Ors on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61844095/
1 1894').

The further prayer is for quashing and setting aside the consequent thereto award No. 37 dated 31.01.2006 (Annexure P-5).
3.

Initially, the institution of the instant writ petition was made in the year 2016, whereas, the above stated respectively made notification(s) and award became issued in the year 2006, thereby, the much belatedly therefroms instituted writ petition before this Court, at the instance of the petitioners, thus constrains this Court, to conclude that therebys the instant writ petition is tainted with a vice of gross delays and laches.
At the outset, the writ petition is declared to be mis- constituted.
4. Be that as it may, on a verdict drawn on 12.10.2020, upon CWP-18718-2016 and connected matters, this Court had declined the relief to the writ petitioners.
However, subsequently the present petitioners instituted a review application bearing No. RA-CW-173- 2021 and in the said review application, the hereinafter extracted order was made on 30.11.2021.

"Learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondent-State of Haryana has filed reply to the review application bringing on record the detailed facts in respect of the averments made in the petition, though it is observed that the petitioners remained absent and did not appear before this Court when the main matter was heard and decided along with bunch of cases nor they disputed the issue of possession raised by the respondents.

However, with a view to do complete justice,
the application to review the order dated 12.10.2020 is allowed and the petition is restored to its original number and is directed to be listed along with bunch of the cases..."
5.

Importantly, the said review was banked upon the factum 2 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086166-DB that at the time of makings of the above referred respective notification(s) and the making of the award, the writ petitioners were not declared as owners of the subject acquisition(s) but they acquired ownership over the subject lands thus post the making of all (supra).
The said claim became founded upon a declaratory decree (Annexure P-6), as became rendered in their favour by the Collector concerned.

6. However, for the reasons to be assigned hereinafter, since at the relevant stage, thus for determining the validity(ies) of the makings of the above stated respective notification(s) and declaration(s) besides qua the validity of the making of the award, thus the contemporaneous thereto revenue records, are the material wherefrom the factum of locus standi of the aggrieved land losers concerned, rather is to be tested.

Moreover, when only therefroms, the trite factum as to whether qua the subject acquisition thus the present petitioners "are persons interested", for thereby theirs ably staking a claim for the compensation amount becoming ordered to be released vis-a-vis them.

Resultantly, if at the stage (supra), thus in the revenue records, the present petitioners were not reflected to be lawful title holders vis-a-vis the subject acquisition(s), as such,
when then they did not acquire any right or locus standi to ask for the quashing of the respectively made notification(s)/declaration(s).
Resultantly the present petitioners are estopped from espousing that the writ reliefs be accorded in their favour.

2 7.

sentences.text:
The reason for the making of the above conclusion becomes sparked from the factum, that since after the completion of 3 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086166-DB acquisition proceedings, or even at the time of the making of a notification under Section 4 of the 'Act of 1894',
thus there is complete vestment of right, title and interest in the acquiring authority vis-a-vis the subject lands.
Moreover, when in consequence theretos, thus the mutation of ownership is attested in favour of the acquiring authority.

In sequel, the acquisition of right, title and interest by the present petitioners, vis-a-vis the subject acquisition, thus through the makings of a declaratory decree (supra), in their favour by the learned Collector concerned, while exercising jurisdiction under Section 11 of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, when is an event which occurred post the making of an award in the year 2006.

Resultantly, they cannot draw any leverage from Annexure P-6, for therebys theirs ably disrobing the validity of conferment of right,
title and interest in the acquiring authority vis-a-vis the subject lands.

8. Moreover, the declaratory suit as became instituted, thus claiming the conferment of ownership rights over the subject acquisitions, was instituted in the year 2013, which is but obviously a date,
thus post the making of an award hence in the year 2005-06 in respect of the subject acquisitions.
The makings of a declaratory decree (Annexure P-6) on the apposite suit happened in the year 2015.

Consequently, both the institution of the apposite suit besides obviously the makings of a verdict thereons, thus post the making of the award but also is to be construed to be a belated endeavour of the petitioners for theirs, rather seeking the bestowment or conferment of right, title and interest qua them over the subject lands.
4 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086166-DB 9

. Moreover, in case the present petitioners conceived, that they had a lawful right, title and interest over the subject acquisitions, therebys they were required to be instituting the said suit prior to the making of the award, and also they were required to be asking for an ad interim injunction, being passed against the acquiring authority, thus for restraining from it, making an award in respect of the subject lands besides were required to be claiming relief, that if an award is made in respect of the suit lands, therebys awaiting the outcome of the civil suit, rather the compensation amount assessed thereunders be not released to the Gram Panchayat concerned.

The omissions (supra) on the part of the petitioners thus in prompt sequel to the initiation of the acquisition proceedings qua the subject lands, climaxes a formidable finding from this Court, that therebys the said belated endeavour on the part of the present petitioners, is merely to frustrate the validly conferred right,
title and interest in the acquiring authority vis-a-vis the subject lands.
Moreover, it also appears that therebys the present petitioners are belatedly attempting to undo the consummated acquisition proceedings, as became launched in respect of the subject acquisitions.
The above belated endeavour is tainted with a vice of gross delay and laches and therebys the instant petition is deemed to be completely mis- constituted.

10. Be that as it may, besides the above evident stark fact, that both the institution of the civil suit and the affirmative verdict made thereons, but occurred post the initiation of the consummated acquisition proceedings, the further stark fact which emerges before 5 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086166-DB this Court, is that, despite at the stage of institution of the suit, the Subhash Sharma & Ors vs State Of Haryana & Ors on 11 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61844095/
3 revenue records detailing the acquiring authority to be owner-in- possession of the subject lands.

sentences.text: Resultantly, when thereby there was a dire necessity for the plaintiffs-petitioners in the civil suit, to cause the impleadment of the acquiring authority as a defendant in the said civil suit.

However, yet the plaintiffs-petitioners before this Court omitted to implead the acquiring authority as a defendant in the civil suit, whereas, its impleadment thereins rather was both just and proper for ensuring the making of a complete adjudication in respect of the entire gamut of the lis.

The further consequence of the said omission, is that, therebys tentatively and, prima facie, the verdict which has been relied upon by the land losers-petitioners before this Court, appears to be obtained through fraud and mis-representation becoming practiced upon the Collector concerned.

In sequel, tentatively besides prima facie at this stage it has no value in law either to defeat or to oust the acquisition of right, title and interest over the subject lands by the acquiring authority.

11. Irrespective of the above, if the present petitioners, have been declared as lawful owners of the subject acquisition(s), thereupon, at this stage, the only right which is to be conferred upon them, is to receive compensation, unless it is already disbursed to the Gram Panchayat concerned, as in terms of the declaratory decree they become "persons interested" to seek a claim for compensation.

12. In aftermath, after dismissing the instant writ petition, this Court directs the Collector concerned, wherebefore whom the compensation assessed under Annexure P-5, is lying deposited,
to in 6 of 7 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:086166-DB terms of the declaratory decree, cause disbursement of the assessed compensation amounts alongwith all the statutory reliefs, vis-a-vis,
the present petitioners but in proportion to their shares in the subject lands.
In case the same is disbursed to the Gram Panchayat concerned thereupon the petitioners may recourse the apt restitutory civil remedy.
13. Since the main case itself has been decided, thus all the pending application(s), if any, also stand(s) disposed of.
(SURESHWAR THAKUR) JUDGE (SUDEEPTI SHARMA) 11.07.2024
JUDGE kavneet singh
Whether speaking/reasoned : Yes/No
Whether reportable : Yes/No 7 of 7
